metaDescription: What to know before hiring a concrete sealing or resurfacing contractor in Ontario, including sealer types, curing time and freeze-thaw protection.
intro: Sealing protects concrete from Ontario's winter cycle of freezing, thawing and road salt, but only if it is applied to fully cured, clean concrete with the right product for the surface. Resurfacing and decorative overlays raise the stakes further, since a poor bond to the existing slab shows up as flaking within a year or two.
whatToLookFor: Correct sealer choice, penetrating versus film-forming, for your slab's exposure
Confirmation that new concrete has cured long enough before sealing
Surface cleaning and profiling before any overlay or resurfacing product goes on
Experience with the specific decorative finish, stamped overlay, stain or broom texture
A maintenance schedule for how often the sealer should be reapplied
typicalCostNotes: Cost depends on square footage, whether it is a straightforward penetrating seal or a full decorative overlay, and how much surface repair or crack filling is needed first, so simple sealing jobs typically cost far less per square foot than resurfacing with a coloured or stamped overlay. Reapplication every few years is normal maintenance rather than a sign of a bad first job, so ask what interval the contractor recommends for your product.
questionsToAsk: Has this concrete cured long enough for the sealer you're recommending?
Is this a penetrating sealer or a film-forming coating, and why for my slab?
How is the surface cleaned and prepped before an overlay is applied?
How often will this sealer or overlay need to be reapplied?
What temperature and weather conditions do you need for the product to cure properly?
redFlags: Wants to seal brand-new concrete before it has finished curing
No surface cleaning or profiling step before a resurfacing overlay
Cannot say which type of sealer they are using or why
